text:
anna: Running a 12h sustained synthetic run against the kv cache harness; seeing steady resident mem growth across shards. baseline process RSS ~8.1GB -> 15.6GB over 12h (~0.63GB/hr).

mike: Ugh. Which workload and kv settings?

anna: Config: 8 shards, seq_len distribution heavy-tail (5% > 64k), reuse enabled, compaction interval default (10m). test cmd:
```
./kvbench --shards=8 --p95-len=32768 --tail=0.05 --duration=12h --reuse=true --compact-interval=600
```

julia: Did you capture kv metrics? eviction_count / page_free_bytes / frag_pct?

anna: Yes. Sample at 6h:
- eviction_count: 4k
- avg_eviction_size: 48KB
- page_free_bytes: 120MB
- frag_pct: 18%
- kv_cache_reuse_hits: 91%
- compactions: 72

mike: frag_pct 18% seems high given reuse=91%. Could be small-slab fragmentation or lots of partial pages. Any evidence of page splitting operations spiking?

anna: I toggled debug logging for page ops. Saw bursts of "split_page" at the 64KB boundary when long-context tokens arrived. timeline snippet:
```
[05:12:12] split_page shard=3 from=65536->32768/32768
[05:12:12] split_page shard=3 from=98304->49152/49152
[05:12:12] free_page shard=3 size=16384
```

julia: That pattern aligns with repeated partial writes into neighbor pages. If the allocator doesn't coalesce freed extents, fragmentation grows over time.

mike: Any difference when increasing compact-interval or forcing compaction more often?

anna: Forced compaction every 60s reduced RSS growth to ~0.08GB/hr but CPU increased ~+14% and tail latency blipped. Short log:
- compaction_forced: 720
- cpu_user_pct: +14
- tail_p95_ms: +18

perf-lab-bot: Automated microbenchmark run complete. baseline vs forced-compact:
- throughput: 54k tok/s -> 51k tok/s (-5.6%)
- mean latency: 12ms -> 13.5ms
- rss_growth_6h: 3.4GB -> 0.43GB

mike: So compacting is effective but costly. We need a middle ground: smarter compaction heuristics (age-aware + fragmentation threshold) rather than time-based.

julia: Agreed. Also suspect the kernel selection path for small-page ops is suboptimal: we're using vectorized copy kernels that allocate temp buffers and cause allocation churn. Need profile.

anna: I attached a heap diff and flamegraph (link): https://perf.redwood/internal/graphs/1998881110/heapdiff.svg
flame shows hotspots in copy_small_pages() and page_split_handling().

mike: Can you run the long-run with KV_USE_COALESCE=1 env var (experimental) and collect same metrics?

anna: Kicked it off with env var. Early numbers (3h): RSS growth 0.25GB/hr, frag_pct 9%, eviction_count down 40%.

julia: Promising. Could be coalescing freed extents reduces fragmentation without frequent compaction. Any regression in correctness?

anna: No correctness regressions observed so far. Ran our replay suite and smoke tests passed.

sre-bot: alert: kv-cache shard-3 mem-residency spike at 1998881210, auto-snapshot saved to s3://redwood-prod/kv/snaps/1998881210.snap

mike: Next steps: 1) run 24h with coalesce enabled, 2) add a new frag-aware compactor that triggers only when frag_pct > 12% and last_compaction_age > 5m, 3) add microbench to measure compaction CPU cost.

julia: I'll prototype frag-aware compactor. API suggestion:
```
struct FragCompactorConfig {
  frag_threshold_pct: u32 = 12;
  min_age_s: u32 = 300;
  max_work_ms: u32 = 200;
}
```

anna: FYI I also saw occasional long tail when compaction coincided with kernel selection switchovers (float16->int8 kernels). Might need to avoid compaction during kernel transitions.

mike: Good catch. Add a compaction inhibit window around kernel_swap events.

perf-lab-bot: Scheduling regression job: kvcache-coalesce-vs-fragcompactor-24h. job id: perf-1998-024. ETA results: 26h.

anna: I'll attach the repro harness and minimal dataset in the ticket: RD-1234. Also saving the debug logs: s3://redwood-internal/kv/debug/1998881110.tar.gz

mike: Great. If frag-aware compaction + coalesce gives similar mem improvements with <8% CPU hit, we can flip it to default on Dedicated.

julia: I'll send a PR with the compactor prototype and feature flag.

anna: Thanks everyone. Will update thread with 24h results. :eyes:

mike: :thumbsup:
